title: Agentic RAG: Retrieval as a Tool
summary: Quick revision notes on agentic RAG: exposing retrieval as a tool the agent calls, rewriting and decomposing queries, multi-hop retrieval, deciding when to retrieve, self-check loops, citing sources, and how failure modes differ from a fixed RAG pipeline.

chapters.title: Agentic RAG: The Mental Model
points: Agentic RAG: the LLM decides whether, what and how often to retrieve by calling a search tool inside its loop, instead of retrieval running once before generation
Fixed RAG pipeline = retrieve once (top-k) → stuff context → generate; agentic RAG = think → call tool → observe → repeat until it can answer
Retrieval tool is just a function schema: name, description, JSON-schema params (query, optional filters, top_k) returning passages with id, text, source
The tool description is the routing prompt: it must say what the corpus contains and when to use it, or the model misuses it
Interview Point: How does agentic RAG differ from fixed RAG? What does the tool schema need so the model calls it correctly? When is fixed RAG still the better choice?

chapters.title: The Agent Retrieval Loop
points: Core loop: model emits tool_call(search, query) → app runs retriever → result returned as tool message → model continues or answers
Cap the loop with max_steps (e.g. 4-6) and a total token budget so it cannot search forever
Return compact results: top 3-5 chunks, trimmed text, stable ids like [doc3#p2] so later answers can cite them
Parallel tool calls let the agent fire several sub-queries in one turn, cutting latency for decomposed questions
Interview Point: Walk through one turn of the tool-calling loop. How do you stop runaway searching? Why return stable chunk ids from the tool?

chapters.title: Query Rewriting, Decomposition and Multi-Hop
points: Rewriting turns a chatty or context-dependent turn into a standalone keyword-rich query (resolve 'it', 'that one' using history)
Decomposition splits a compound question into independent sub-queries, run in parallel: 'Compare A and B pricing' → 'A pricing', 'B pricing'
Multi-hop: later queries depend on earlier answers, so they run sequentially: 'CEO of company that acquired X' → find acquirer → then find its CEO
Fixed pipeline embeds the raw question once and misses the second hop because the bridge entity never appears in the question
Use independent sub-queries for parallel fan-out; use dependent hops only when query N needs the result of N-1
Interview Point: When do you decompose vs do multi-hop? Why does single-shot top-k fail on multi-hop questions? How do you resolve pronouns in follow-up questions?

chapters.title: Deciding When to Retrieve and Self-Check Loops
points: Skip retrieval for chit-chat, math, general knowledge, or when the answer is already in context; retrieve for private, recent or specific facts
Routing is learned from the tool description plus a system rule such as 'search before answering any question about company docs'
Self-check: after retrieving, the agent grades whether passages actually answer the question (relevant / partial / irrelevant)
On a weak grade, re-retrieve with a rewritten query, a broader or narrower filter, or a different source; stop after N retries and say 'not found'
Final groundedness check: verify each claim is supported by a retrieved passage, and drop or flag unsupported claims
Interview Point: How does the agent decide not to retrieve? What triggers a re-retrieval and what stops it? How do you check an answer is grounded?

chapters.title: Citing Sources and Failure Modes vs Fixed RAG
points: Citations: require inline markers like [doc3#p2] that map to ids returned by the tool, and render them as links or footnotes
Validate citations in code: every cited id must exist in the tool results of this run, or the answer is rejected and regenerated
Fixed RAG failures: one-shot recall miss, irrelevant top-k stuffed into context, no recovery, cannot do multi-hop
Agentic RAG failures: looping on the same query, over-retrieving (extra latency and cost), skipping retrieval and hallucinating, dropping the question mid-decomposition
Mitigations: step cap, dedupe repeated queries, log every tool call and trace it, evaluate with answer correctness plus citation precision
Interview Point: How do you prevent fabricated citations? Name two failure modes unique to agentic RAG and their fixes. What do you measure to compare agentic vs fixed RAG?

chapters.title: Agentic RAG Cheat Sheet
points: Pattern: tool_call(search) → observe → answer or retry; cap with max_steps
Tool schema: name, corpus-describing description, query/filters/top_k, returns id+text+source
Rewrite for standalone queries; decompose for parallel; hop for dependent
Retrieve for private or recent facts; skip for chit-chat, math, in-context answers
Grade relevance → rewrite and retry → stop at N and admit 'not found'
Cite stable ids and validate each against this run's tool results
Fixed RAG fails silently on misses; agentic RAG fails by looping or skipping: cap, dedupe, trace
Interview Point: Summarize when you would choose agentic over fixed RAG. What guardrails make an agent loop production-safe?
